release_contents:
Two feature bodies of work, both on main since the last deploy (8078f74), shipped together in this one release per an explicit owner decision to not gate Mail Center on finishing Phase 3 translation first:

(1) PHASE 3 — Bilingual Admin UI/UX foundation (commit 971da35). Admin locale switcher (বাংলা | English) with NO new /admin routes — same URLs, locale resolved via SetAdminLocale middleware (user.ui_locale column -> session -> cookie -> bn default), persisted via POST /locale (LocaleController). Full lang/{bn,en}/admin.php + lang/{bn,en}/statuses.php catalogues covering: sidebar/nav, dashboard (controller-level strings converted, not just views), header, auth/login/reset-password (including the login page's own switcher, added after a screenshot caught it missing from the guest layout), profile, all error pages (403/404/419/429/500/503), forms/buttons/pagination/flash/empty-states, status labels. bn_date()/bn_month_name()/bn_number() etc. helpers made locale-aware without renaming any of their ~98 existing call sites. AdminTranslationParityTest (5 tests) asserts bn/en key parity and that no English value was left as its Bangla original. KNOWN INCOMPLETE, reported to the owner as such: ~50 module view files and ~62 PHP files still contain hardcoded Bangla not yet run through the bulk-localization tooling — English-mode admins will see a mix of translated chrome and untranslated Bangla content on those specific pages until that work continues. The `[বাংলা][English]` tabbed bilingual editor component (for the `_en` fields from the earlier Phase 2 content model) has NOT been built yet — those forms still use the old stacked bn-then-en layout. Bangla-mode behavior (the default for every admin) is 100% unchanged.

(2) MAIL CENTER — backend data layer + webhook path (commits 62716f1/edf1c12). hostinger/mail-api-php-sdk installed; HostingerMailService wraps it (mailboxes/folders/messages/send/reply/forward/webhooks), every method verified against the actual generated SDK source rather than guessed. mail:discover verifies GET /me and lists accessible mailboxes without ever printing the token. New POST /api/webhooks/hostinger-mail (outside the /v1 contract, api middleware group, no CSRF) receives Hostinger's message.received webhook: bearer-secret auth via hash_equals(), idempotent via mail_webhook_events' unique hostinger_event_id, NEVER logs or persists message subject/body. mail:webhook:register / mail:webhook:test commands implement the register-then-verify-before-notifications sequence the owner specified; the returned webhook secret is written directly to .env, never printed/logged. AdminNotification/AdminNotificationRead models + AdminNotificationService: notifications store type+meta only, title/body resolved PER VIEWER at display time from the lang catalogue, so one event renders correctly regardless of the viewing admin's own locale. New 'mail' RBAC permission module (view/read/send/manage/delete), default-deny except super_admin. NOT YET BUILT: Mail Center UI (inbox/compose/reply/forward), bell/mail badge UI, real-time delivery, notification sound.

TWO REAL BUGS CAUGHT BEFORE THIS DEPLOY, BY THIS DEPLOY'S OWN PIPELINE: (a) admin_notifications.title was non-nullable in the migration despite AdminNotificationService intentionally never setting it (title is resolved from lang files, not stored) — caught by this session's own new feature test, fixed in the migration before staging. (b) HostingerMailService was bound as a container singleton whose factory threw immediately when no token was configured — meaning isConfigured() itself was unreachable in ANY environment without the token, including this very build's own isolated test-tree copy (no .env). Fixed to construct with an empty token instead of throwing; a real API call against an unconfigured instance now fails naturally instead of the class failing at injection time. Regression test added (HostingerMailServiceUnconfiguredTest).

switch_note: Clean switch at 2026-09-26T18:05:03Z: ok:true, atomic_rename_ms 0.22, public_asset_sync_ms 47.6, routes_changed TRUE (routes/api.php and routes/web.php both changed — route:cache correctly ran), all cache rebuilds exit 0.
post_deploy_production_e2e: Verified directly against the live site after switch: (1) POST /api/webhooks/hostinger-mail with no Authorization header -> 401, confirming the new webhook receiver route is live and correctly gated. (2) Guest-level locale switch verified round-trip with real cookies: GET /login default renders বাংলা ('প্রশাসনিক লগইন') -> POST /locale locale=en -> 302 + new provatferi_admin_locale cookie -> GET /login now renders English ('Sign in') -> POST /locale locale=bn -> GET /login renders বাংলা again correctly. (3) 404 route returns 404. NOT YET DONE: the fully-authenticated multi-module E2E from the owner's own Phase 3 spec (admin login -> switch English -> navigate modules -> edit an English translation -> save -> reload -> DB-backed ui_locale persistence -> switch back to Bangla) — this needs real admin credentials or a temp QA account, neither of which this session created (per standing guidance: never rotate the Super Admin password for QA access).
critical_finding_not_yet_resolved: mail:discover run directly in production (via one-shot cron against artisan on the live laravel-admin/ path) reports: 'HOSTINGER_MAIL_API_TOKEN is not set in this environment's .env — nothing to verify.' This contradicts an earlier report that the token had been added to both .env files — it is genuinely absent from production's .env right now. This is an owner-only blocker: the token value is never held by this session (by design, per the standing 'never print/log/commit the token' constraint) and must be added directly to domains/provatferi.org/laravel-admin/.env on the server by the owner. Everything downstream (mail:discover, mail:webhook:register, mail:webhook:test, and the Mail Center itself) is deployed and ready — it will work the moment the token is actually present. The contract-check step surfaced this correctly during the build (reported services.hostinger_mail.token as 'present_but_null', not 'missing' — the config key exists, its env-sourced value does not) and did not block the deploy since an unconfigured mail integration is a valid, non-fatal state by design (see the HostingerMailService fix above).

Changed: MX record repointed from smtp.google.com (priority 1) to mx1.hostinger.com (priority 5); new MX record added for mx2.hostinger.com (priority 10); SPF TXT changed from 'v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:_spf.mail.hostinger.com ~all' to 'v=spf1 include:_spf.mail.hostinger.com ~all'. Untouched: DKIM (hostingermail-a/b/c CNAMEs), DMARC (p=none, already had a rua= reporting address), autoconfig/autodiscover CNAMEs, google-site-verification TXT, all website A/CNAME records. This was a DNS-only mail-routing fix -- no website/CDN/routing change. (Historical — carried from the previous deploy record, not touched this deploy.)
cron_timing_note: Cron runs in UTC. One-shot crons scheduled 5-8 minutes ahead on specific minutes, read once via getCronJobOutputV1, then deleted immediately — none left armed (verified empty via listAccountCronJobsV1 after the switch step). One real multi-hour wall-clock jump occurred during this deploy's waits (10:32->17:49 UTC) between the migrate-check and smoke-test-isolated checks — not an error, just elapsed real time during a long session; the scheduled cron had already fired and completed long before it was checked.
release_manager_path_reminder: release-manager.php lives at the PRIVATE path /home/u951246149/domains/provatferi.org/laravel-admin-releases/_tooling/release-manager.php for every step after the one-time install — NOT under public_html/admin/. Release ids use the SERVER's own format (sha-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS-ish, confirmed via that release's manifest.json under _release_staging/), not the local build folder's timezone-local timestamp.
never_fetch_a_staged_script_url: Requesting a staged one-shot script's URL EXECUTES it (it is under the web-servable docroot). Verify removal with the file listing tool instead.
local_mariadb_note: The local dev build machine's MariaDB (XAMPP) was found stopped partway through this deploy, causing one build-release.sh run to hang indefinitely (not fail fast) waiting on a DB connection rather than erroring — the two php.exe worker processes showed real but very slow memory growth, which read as 'still working' until a longer observation window showed it was actually stalled. Fixed by starting D:\ISDB-BISEW\xampp\mysql_start.bat and killing the orphaned php.exe processes before rebuilding. Future sessions: confirm mysqld.exe is running before trusting a long-silent build-release.sh run. (Historical note, carried forward — MariaDB was already confirmed running before this deploy's own build.)
curl_csrf_testing_note: When scripting a POST to a CSRF-protected route (e.g. /locale) with curl, fetch the CSRF token and set the cookie jar in the SAME request that will be reused for the POST, not across separate GET calls with the jar re-opened each time — doing it in two disjoint GET calls produced a spurious 419 in this session even though the actual endpoint was working correctly (confirmed immediately after by doing the GET-then-POST as a tighter single-jar sequence).
